file_roles.evidence: The error is a missing conversion between two types this header defines, "cannot convert argument 1 from 'const QTypedArrayData<T>::iterator' to 'QTypedArrayData<T>::const_iterator'", with the compiler stating that nothing supplies it, 'No user-defined-conversion operator available that can perform this conversion, or the operator cannot be called'. The call site that needs it, qvector.h, is not in the gold set; the only non-test source file the fix changed is the header that owns QTypedArrayData::iterator and ::const_iterator, so the missing conversion is the wrong logic and it lives here.

rationale: The failure surfaces where the conversion is needed, 'qtbase/src/corelib/tools/qvector.h(331): error C2664', inside 'while compiling class template member function int QVector<QItemSelectionRange>::removeAll(const T &)', reached from 'qtbase\\src\\corelib\\itemmodels\\qitemselectionmodel.h(244)'. Neither of those files is gold. The one gold file defines the iterator types named in the error, so the caller in qvector.h fails on a conversion the callee's type never offered.
notes: The packet renders this file's diff as '(no diff retrieved)', so no hunk could be cited for any gold file in this instance. The report names a culprit commit rather than a location, 'After c946b07d9c2023c56ec3cae3ef8a425d12f8d7df, Qt no longer compiles on MSVC2019', which is the bisect-style evidence CONVENTIONS records for MDEV-21063 and MDEV-21195. The gold file does not appear in the reported output at all: the error names qvector.h and qitemselectionmodel.h by path and qarraydata.h only through the type names 'QTypedArrayData<T>::iterator' and 'QTypedArrayData<T>::const_iterator'. The header is labelled causal under the CONVENTIONS header rule because the correction it must carry is a conversion operator with a body, not a declaration; the diff would confirm that. The instance has no runtime failure; it is a compile break on one compiler, 'MSVC2019', and the pasted text is compiler and NMAKE output, not a program log.
